PQDM implements published methods for the evaluation of long-term power
quality measurements. This vignette shows the data format, the preparation of
the data and how the methods are chained. Each method is described in detail
on its help page, which also names the publication it is based on.

```{r setup}
library(PQDM)
```

## Data format

All methods work on weekly 95th percentiles of 10-minute values in long
format, one row per site, voltage level, phase, parameter and week:

| Column    | Content                                                  |
|-----------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `site`    | measurement site                                         |
| `voltage` | voltage level or nominal voltage, e.g. `"MV"` or `"20 kV"` |
| `week`    | Monday of the ISO calendar week, class `Date`            |
| `phase`   | phase or line-to-line voltage, e.g. `"L1"`               |
| `param`   | power quality parameter, e.g. `"H5"` for the 5th harmonic |
| `value`   | weekly 95th percentile                                   |

Missing weeks are marked by `NA` or simply left out. The package contains the
synthetic data set `pq_weekly_example` with the 3rd and 5th harmonic and Plt
of 24 fictitious medium-voltage sites from 2022 to 2025; each measurement
follows one typical course, e.g. a summer season or a rising trend (see
`?pq_weekly_example`):

```{r}
head(pq_weekly_example)
```

## Workflow

A typical analysis consists of three stages:

1. **Data:** `pq_validate()` checks the data and assesses the data
   availability, `pq_fill()` fills gaps where a method needs complete time
   series.
2. **Methods:** one function per method, e.g. `pq_quality_reserve()`,
   `pq_season()` or `pq_trend()`.
3. **Results:** `print()` for an overview and `summary()` for the result
   table of each method; `summary(x, by = ...)` aggregates the quality
   reserve into indices.

The stages are chained with the pipe:

```{r}
tr <- pq_weekly_example |>
  pq_validate() |>
  pq_fill() |>
  pq_trend()
tr
```

## Validation

`pq_validate()` checks the format, sets invalid values (`0`, `NaN`, `Inf`) to
`NA`, completes the weekly grid and determines for each time series the
measurement duration, the share of missing weeks and the longest gap. Time
series that do not meet the criteria of a method are marked, not removed.

```{r}
v <- pq_validate(pq_weekly_example)
v
```

The data availability per time series is in `v$series`, together with one
logical column per method:

```{r}
head(v$series)
```

The criteria can be changed; the defaults are:

| Method            | Minimum duration | Longest gap | Share of missing weeks |
|-------------------|------------------|-------------|------------------------|
| quality reserve   | 1 week           | –           | –                      |
| season            | 52 weeks         | 10 weeks    | 20 %                   |
| trend             | 53 weeks         | 10 weeks    | 20 %                   |
| forecast          | 157 weeks        | 10 weeks    | 20 %                   |

```{r}
pq_validate(pq_weekly_example, max_gap = 4, max_missing = 0.1)
```

## Filling gaps

Seasonal variation, trend and forecast need complete time series.
`pq_fill()` fills the gaps within each time series by linear interpolation
and marks the filled weeks in the column `filled`:

```{r}
v <- pq_fill(v)
v

s20 <- v$data[v$data$site == "S20" & v$data$param == "H5" &
                v$data$phase == "L1", ]
plot(s20$week, s20$value, type = "l", xlab = "Week", ylab = "H5 in %",
     main = "S20, H5, L1: weekly 95th percentiles")
points(s20$week[s20$filled], s20$value[s20$filled], col = "red", pch = 19)
```

The methods that need complete series call `pq_fill()` themselves if the data
have not been filled yet, so the explicit call is optional. The quality
reserve ignores filled weeks, because an interpolated week is not a
measurement.

## Methods

| Function               | Method                                            |
|------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `pq_quality_reserve()` | quality reserve with respect to user-supplied limits |
| `pq_season()`          | identification and quantification of seasonal variations |
| `pq_trend()`           | trend components and recent trend gains           |

Each method accepts either the result of `pq_validate()` or the raw data in
long format, in which case the validation is called internally.

## Limits

Limits from standards such as EN 50160 or IEC 61000-2-2 are not included in
the package. Where a method needs limits, they are supplied by the user, e.g.
from the applicable standard or from planning levels of the network operator.
